items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: He came down with his wife, Lucille, to hear us.

ctx.x: And when we got there, he had his right hand man put on a bunch of records, and we settled back and listened to Louis, and he played nothing but Bobby Hackett records. Well, we sort of hinted that we'd like to hear some of his records.

Then when I was with the Peanuts Hucko Quartet at the Roosevelt Grill, Louis had been real sick towards the end, and he was recuperating. He came down with his wife, Lucille, to hear us. Peanuts had been with Louis for a long time -- he did some of those lengthy world wide trips with him. He made some movies with him, and that was a few years back, and Louis got up for nostalgia's sake, I couldn't believe it -- and he was a little bit weak, but he had that beautiful grin, and he came up on the bandstand and sang…

Afterwards, he had Lou McGarity and Peanuts and myself over to his table and he said, "Lucille, by my judge and witness; when I reorganize and I get to feel better, I want these three boys in my band" -- and he says,
